static_traits.name: Fang Fei
static_traits.family_status: Has a son who plays soccer; tense relationship with the son and more quarrels due to negative thoughts about his performance
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no prior psychotherapy; has not yet had similar problems before
static_traits.language_features: Self-reported anxiety, racing thoughts; clear expression, good cooperative attitude; able to identify and discuss own negative thinking; quickly returning to negative content after mentioning positive fragments

basic_info.main_problem: I feel anxious and upset about my son's soccer performance. After the team's losing streak at the season start, I only focus on his negative performance and compare him with other players; these negative thoughts appear at every game or practice, causing persistent emotional distress.
basic_info.core_demands: I seek counseling because I realize the negative thoughts about my son's soccer performance are affecting my daily life and causing significant pain. I hope to view his ability more balancedly, thereby reducing anxiety.

special_situations.event: Son's team starting to lose consecutively at the season's start
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If the team keeps losing, it means my son isn't good enough and won't get better in the future
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Tries to encourage the son and deliberately focus on the positive, but inwardly continues to worry and compare

special_situations.event: The son missed a key goal in a match
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If mistakes happen at key moments, it proves he's not good enough and lets the team down
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: More frequently compares him with other team members, while verbally trying to encourage him
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: He let the team down; all other teammates are stronger than him

special_situations.event: Comparing the son's performance with teammates
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Falling short of others equals failure, meaning not good enough
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Constantly comparing his gap with other players
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: He's not as good as others

special_situations.event: The son assisted and scored in a game, but the team ultimately lost
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only winning counts as good; positive performances don't matter in the face of failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Ignores or belittles positive moments and continues to focus on setbacks

core_conflict.wish: Longing for my son to excel at soccer, maintaining a harmonious intimate relationship with him, and being a supportive good mother myself
core_conflict.fear: Fearing my son's continued failure, fearing my own worries and inappropriate reactions will hurt his confidence and worsen the relationship
defense_goal: Gaining a sense of control by fixating on the negative and comparing, reducing anxiety from uncertainty

object_relations.self_representation: Anxious and harsh mother, worrying about not being supportive enough
object_relations.object_representation: A son needing improvement, easily disappointing others

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When invited in counseling to focus on the positive side and try a more balanced perspective
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing that focusing too much on the positive equals denying reality (the team keeps losing), and that letting my guard down will make things worse
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Emphasizing the 'facts' of losses and mistakes, using a cautious yet firm tone, persistently pointing out problems, and downplaying positive evidence.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When thinking of her son's key mistake in a game or the team's loss
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Simplifying complex team performance into my son's personal failure, to avoid touching my own helplessness and uncertainty
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using absolutist language like 'never will' 'not good enough', ignoring middle ground and positive evidence.

manifestations: Having friends but not yet confiding worries about my son's performance to them
Keeps worries hidden in his heart; hard to communicate openly with his son
outcomes: Subjective sense of burden and increased sense of isolation

manifestations: Feels 'everything revolves around the son's performance'
Difficulty deriving pleasure from other activities
outcomes: Narrowed life experience, reduced subjective sense of meaning

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Self-blame: believing I may 'not have done enough to support him'
Cares excessively about winning and losing and comparisons, carefully controls his focus
Not discussing worries with friends, shrinking social support

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'.
manifestations: Mainly blames the team's loss on the son's performance
Believes 'he let the team down' and places the negative evaluation on his son

contact_model.definition: The individual ignores or avoids a stimulus from the internal or external environment, deliberately avoiding direct contact, corresponding to 'acceptance'.
manifestations: After mentioning the joy of an assist, quickly turns back to the loss and negative content
When talking about positive moments, difficult to stay with them; quickly slides into a problem-focused narrative

exception_events.target_problem: When watching my son's games or practices, the client is typically occupied by negative thoughts, feeling anxious, struggling to experience the positive or enjoy the process.
exception_events.unique_outcome: In one competition, her son assisted and scored; at that moment she felt sincere pride and happiness, briefly breaking the negative cycle.
exception_events.reason: Different attention and understanding: at the time she focused on her son's specific contributions rather than only the final score, allowing her to experience positive emotions; a subsequent team loss refocused her on the negative.

positive_force: Willing to seek professional help and cooperate with counseling
Able to identify and articulate own negative thinking
Motivated to support and encourage son
Able to notice positive moments (such as pride when making an assist)
negative_force: Mental filtering and disqualifying the positive
Not yet using friend support, staying silent causing subjective isolation
Tense relationship with the son, emotional interactions intensifying anxiety

target_behavior.behavior: Excessive worry and repeated negative thinking in situations related to the son's competition
antecedent: Before and during competitions or training
The son's key mistake (e.g. missing a goal)
target_behavior.core_reason: Cognitive distortions (catastrophizing, all-or-nothing, overgeneralization, mental filtering, disqualifying the positive) and external comparison jointly causing over-interpretation of failure and maintained anxiety
target_behavior.function: Gaining a subjective sense of control over uncontrollable situations, preventing imagined worse outcomes (avoiding uncertainty)
target_behavior.consequence: Persistent anxiety and depression, tense relationship with the son, difficulty enjoying other activities, daily mood and quality of life affected
